also: from now on I’ll speak Latin

evidence: M-O s.v. speak: do you speak Latin?
terms.comment: The adverb names the language; for modern ones see in English, in Bulgarian, in Portuguese. Lewis & Short notes that Latīnē loquī can also mean to speak good, plain Latin (Cic. Brut. 166).

evidence: Cic. Brut. 140: nōn enim tam praeclārum est scīre Latīnē quam turpe nescīre

phrases.latin: nōn tamen hoc adeō superstitiōsē fierī velim, ut diū tantum Graecē loquātur aut discat, sīcut plērīsque mōris est
phrases.english: But I would not have this done so rigidly that he speaks or learns only Greek for a long time, as most people do.

phrases.latin: nōn enim tam praeclārum est scīre Latīnē quam turpe nescīre
phrases.english: For knowing Latin is not so much a credit as not knowing it is a disgrace.

phrases.latin: scīs enim mē Graecē loquī in Latīnō sermōne nōn plūs solēre quam in Graecō Latīnē
phrases.english: For you know I am no more in the habit of speaking Greek in a Latin conversation than Latin in a Greek one.
Do you know how to speak Latin?
Since when have you been learning Latin?
Who is able to write Latin?

phrases.latin: Latīnam linguam discō; aliquantum jam intellegō, sed nōndum expedītē loquor.
phrases.english: I’m learning Latin; I understand a fair amount already, but I don’t speak it fluently yet.

phrases.latin: Ipse mihi videor jam dēdidicisse Latīnē: nam didicī Geticē Sarmaticēque loquī.
phrases.english: I feel I have unlearned my Latin by now, for I have learned to speak Getic and Sarmatian.

phrases.latin: Quid ais tū? ecquid commeministī Pūnicē? — Nihil edepol.
phrases.english: Tell me, do you remember any Punic? — Not a word, honestly.

phrases.latin: nōn tamen ut aut loquerētur expedītē aut compōnere aliquid audēret
phrases.english: (he studied Greek) but not to the point of speaking it fluently or venturing to write anything in it

phrases.latin: At ut sciās, nunc dehinc Latīnē jam loquar.
phrases.english: But so that you know, from now on I’ll speak Latin.

sources: Lewis & Short: loquor · Lewis & Short: Latinus · Lewis & Short: Graeci · Lewis & Short: scio
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 30, 337, 358.
